In [[mathematics]] and [[control theory]], '''zero dynamics''' describes the internal behavior of a dynamic system when its outputs are constrained to [[zero]] through control inputs (e.g., maintaining a robot arm at a fixed position while internal states continue to evolve).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Van de Straete |first1=H.J. |last2=Youcef-Toumi |first2=K. |date=June 1996 |title=Physical Meaning of Zeros and Transmission Zeros from Bond Graph Models |journal=IFAC Proceedings Volumes |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=4422–4427 |doi=10.1016/s1474-6670(17)58377-9 |hdl=1721.1/11140 |issn=1474-6670 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> Even when outputs are held at zero, the system's internal dynamics may persist, influencing stability and performance. 

Understanding zero dynamics helps design robust controllers in applications like [[robotics]], [[feedback linearization]], and [[control engineering]].

== History ==
The idea was introduced thirty years ago as the [[Nonlinear optics|nonlinear]] approach to the concept of transmission of zeros. The original purpose of introducing the concept was to develop an [[Asymptote|asymptotic]] stabilization with a set of guaranteed regions of attraction ([[Semi-global matching|semi-global]] [[Controllability|stabilizability]]), to make the overall system stable.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Isidori|first=Alberto|date=September 2013|title=The zero dynamics of a nonlinear system: From the origin to the latest progresses of a long successful story|journal=European Journal of Control|volume=19|issue=5|pages=369–378|doi=10.1016/j.ejcon.2013.05.014|s2cid=15277067 |issn=0947-3580}}</ref>

== Initial working ==
Given the internal dynamics of any system, zero dynamics refers to the control action chosen in which the output variables of the system are kept identically zero.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Youcef-Toumi|first1=K.|last2=Wu|first2=S-T|title=1991 American Control Conference |chapter=Input/Output Linearization using Time Delay Control |date=June 1991|pages=2601–2606|publisher=IEEE|doi=10.23919/acc.1991.4791872|isbn=0-87942-565-2|s2cid=20562917 }}</ref> While various systems have an equally distinctive set of zeros, such as decoupling zeros, invariant zeros, and transmission zeros, the reason for developing this concept was to control the non-minimum phase and nonlinear systems effectively.<ref>{{Citation|chapter=Control Theory|pages=91–149|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|doi=10.1007/3-540-45436-5_5|isbn=978-3-540-42626-4|title=Analytic and Geometric Study of Stratified Spaces|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|year=2001|volume=1768 }}</ref>

== Applications ==
The concept is widely utilized in SISO mechanical systems, whereby applying a few [[heuristic]] approaches, zeros can be identified for various linear systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Miu|first=D. K.|date=1991-09-01|title=Physical Interpretation of Transfer Function Zeros for Simple Control Systems With Mechanical Flexibilities|journal=Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement, and Control|volume=113|issue=3|pages=419–424|doi=10.1115/1.2896426|issn=0022-0434}}</ref> Zero dynamics adds an essential feature to the overall system’s analysis and the design of the controllers. Mainly its behavior plays a significant role in measuring the performance limitations of specific feedback systems. In a [[Single-input single-output system|Single Input Single Output system]], the zero dynamics can be identified by using junction structure patterns. In other words, using concepts like [[bond graph]] models can help to point out the potential direction of the SISO systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Huang|first1=S.Y.|last2=Youcef-Toumi|first2=K.|date=June 1996|title=Zero Dynamics of Nonlinear MIMO Systems from System Configurations - A Bond Graph Approach|journal=IFAC Proceedings Volumes|volume=29|issue=1|pages=4392–4397|doi=10.1016/s1474-6670(17)58372-x|issn=1474-6670|doi-access=}}</ref>

Apart from its application in nonlinear standardized systems, similar controlled results can be obtained by using zero dynamics on nonlinear discrete-time systems. In this scenario, the application of zero dynamics can be an interesting tool to measure the performance of nonlinear digital design systems (nonlinear discrete-time systems).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Monaco|first1=S.|last2=Normand-Cyrot|first2=D.|author2-link= Dorothée Normand-Cyrot |date=September 1988|title=Zero dynamics of sampled nonlinear systems|journal=Systems & Control Letters|volume=11|issue=3|pages=229–234|doi=10.1016/0167-6911(88)90063-1|issn=0167-6911}}</ref>

Before the advent of zero dynamics, the problem of acquiring non-interacting control systems by using internal stability was not specifically discussed. However, with the [[asymptotic stability]] present within the zero dynamics of a system, static feedback can be ensured. Such results make zero dynamics an interesting tool to guarantee the internal stability of non-interacting control systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Isidori|first1=A.|last2=Grizzle|first2=J.W.|date=October 1988|title=Fixed modes and nonlinear noninteracting control with stability|journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control|volume=33|issue=10|pages=907–914|doi=10.1109/9.7244|bibcode=1988ITAC...33..907I |issn=0018-9286}}</ref>
